-121.99000,37.77250.name: Reproductive Science Center of the San Francisco Bay Area
-121.99000,37.77250.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Mary D. Hinckley, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

100.60000,14.08000.name: BIOTEC — National Center for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology
100.60000,14.08000.desc: Thailand’s national biotechnology centre, working on rice, shrimp and cassava. Thailand permits no commercial GM cultivation while conducting substantial research, which is a common arrangement and one that leaves a national capability with nowhere domestic to go.

5.32400,60.39000.name: Benchmark Genetics
5.32400,60.39000.desc: Breeds salmon, shrimp and tilapia for aquaculture worldwide, using genomic selection and disease-resistance programmes. Farmed salmon is among the most intensively bred animals on Earth, and escapes into wild rivers make that breeding an environmental question rather than an agricultural one.

26.21400,-29.12110.name: ACB v Minister of Agriculture and Monsanto
26.21400,-29.12110.state: Bloemfontein — Supreme Court of Appeal of South Africa
26.21400,-29.12110.desc: Nine years of litigation, ended in October 2024 by a full bench of five judges setting aside several layers of decision-making behind the commercial release of drought-tolerant maize MON87460. The permit had been granted in June 2015 and appealed within two months; the High Court dismissed the challenge in 2023 and the Supreme Court of Appeal set that judgment aside too, including its findings on the precautionary principle. The argument was administrative rather than scientific: that the executive council had accepted the applicant's evidence uncritically and disregarded the contrary expert evidence put before it. Three things make this the most useful case on the map for a reader outside Europe and North America — it was brought by a small non-profit with legal aid, it succeeded on how the decision was made rather than on proving harm, and it took nine years, which is the real price of that route.

-122.31300,47.66000.name: Seattle Sperm Bank
-122.31300,47.66000.desc: One of the larger US donor sperm providers, and included here to complete the shape of the market rather than for any single event. The American picture is a handful of large commercial banks with family limits in the tens, one non-profit at ten, and a federal government that sets no limit at all and keeps no register of how many children any donor has fathered. A prospective parent choosing between banks is therefore choosing between private policies, and the number of half-siblings their child will have is a term of business rather than a matter of law.
